title: Sequence affinity fusion probe
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working investigation into how per-request sequence characteristics (particularly mixture of short prefixes + long generation and sequence-homogeneous batches) change kernel selection and fused-op behavior across FlashAttention vs paged attention (FlashPaged) implementations and our fused-ops stack. Goal: find micro-policy adjustments to routing/priming that reduce p95/p99 tail without increasing median > 5% and avoid destabilizing fusedop quantization paths.

Why this matters right now:
- Several production customers on Dedicated reported intermittent p99 spikes when a small fraction of requests have long decode lengths (>=1024) interleaved with many short requests (<=64).
- Our heuristics currently choose FlashAttention by default for model variants with kernel support, with a paged fallback for extremely long contexts or memory pressure. But observed kernel handoffs at runtime cause glints in latency and occasional OOM-like retries.

Hypothesis (sequence-affinity):
- Kernel selection is overly sensitive to short transient long sequences arriving on a shared GPU; the runtime will flip to paged/flashpaged kernels or fused-op variants mid-batch, leaving some microbatches executed with different memory/layout assumptions => cache invalidation + register pressure => tail latency spikes.
- For mixed-length batches, performing early sequence-affinity grouping (coalesce by expected generation length and prefix length) before kernel selection will reduce kernel-churn and stabilize warp occupancy, improving p99.

Experiments run (notes, commands, and quick results):
1) Baseline trace collection (no grouping)
- Date: 2025-11-04
- Workload: 80% queries with length 16, 20% with generated length target 1024, arrival Poisson (lambda 200 qps), batch scheduler configured to 16 max tokens per microbatch.
- Trace: runtime_trace_20251104.json (collected via tracebench)
- Observed (median / p95 / p99 per-token ms): 0.82 / 3.4 / 12.7
- Kernel switches observed: average 2.3 kernel handoffs per-second per-GPU, often coinciding with long request start times.

2) FlashPinned policy: force FlashAttention unless OOM predicted, disable paged fallback until memory > 92%
- Date: 2025-11-07
- Result: median 0.87 (+6%), p95 3.8, p99 16.4 (worse).
- Notes: Flash pinned caused queueing/backpressure and large stalls when a single long request appeared; garbage collection of KV caches and register spills seemed to occur.

3) Sequence-affinity batching: pre-grouping step that collects microrequests for up to 5ms or until count threshold, group by expected total sequence (prefix+gen target) into short-group (<=128) and long-group (>=512). Kernel selection then performed per-group.
- Date: 2025-12-02
- Result: median 0.84, p95 2.9, p99 7.1 (improvement vs baseline p99 -44%).
- Tradeoff: 5ms added head-of-line delay for grouping; decreased overall kernel handoffs to ~0.7/sec/GPU.

4) Mixed fused-op quantized path probe: enabled fused LayerNorm+MatMul fused op when using FlashAttention; disabled when running paged. This test toggles fused-ops at runtime when kernel selection flips (simulate current behavior)
- Date: 2026-01-12
- Result: p99 19.2 (severe).
- Root cause: switching fused-op kernels changes memory layout expectations (fp16 vs q4a temp buffers) causing extra copies and kernel-serialization.

5) FlashPaged affinity (hybrid): use grouping above, but for long-group we use FlashPaged with larger microbatch tokens and explicit KV prefetching; for short-group use FlashAttention fused path. Add KV priming for the long-group requests to warm local cache before kernel heavy path.
- Date: 2026-02-18
- Result: median 0.81, p95 2.6, p99 5.9. CPU overhead small. Reduced fusion churn and eliminated the pathological spikes in step 4.

Telemetry artifacts and what we recorded:
- tracebench timelines (attached ids in linked_artifacts)
- gpu-sched logs showing kernel launch names and occupancy
- nvprof-style sampling snapshots with register pressure and l2 misses
- host-side copy/cuda-memcpy timings
- per-request sequence metadata added to traces: (prefix_len, gen_target, chosen_kernel, fused_ops_path, kv_prefetch_count)

Notable low-level observations:
- Register pressure increases by ~18% when switching between fused-op and non-fused-op paths mid-queue; the kernel scheduler introduces serializing fences to drain and re-bind descriptors that show as 1-3ms stalls in host timeline.
- FlashPaged has higher per-token overhead at small seq lengths (<64) due to page table traversal and microkernel set-up; FlashAttention shines for short sequences but is fragile under sudden long sequence arrival.
- KV prefetch (issuing small warmup microbatches to populate KV cache) reduced page faults on the FlashPaged path by ~70% for long-group samples.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- How to set grouping delay budget adaptively? 5ms worked in our testbed, but under higher qps this may increase headroom violations. We should simulate higher load (1k qps) and tune grouping thresholds.
- Can we make fused-op kernels tolerant of alternate memory layouts so mid-queue toggles don't force copies? This might require ABI-stable buffer descriptors or dual-path kernels that detect layout cheaply.
- Cost tradeoff: sequence-affinity grouping increases queuing but reduces p99. We need to quantify end-to-end SLA impact for customer plans (Hosted vs Dedicated).

Action items (short term):
- [Ava] Push a prototype of sequence-affinity coalescer into runtime feature-flagged gate (PR referenced in linked artifacts).
- [Diego] Add microbench harness to simulate 1k qps mixed workloads and sweep grouping delay 1/3/5/10ms.
- [Ruth] Prototype layout-insensitive fused op shim. Assess performance delta on NV hardware family A100/V100/H100.
- [Liam] Add trace annotation for 'kernel-switch-reason' and surface in Console per-route latency breakdown.

Design notes for implementation:
- Keep grouping shallow and localized to the scheduling thread to avoid global head-of-line effects. Use a 3-tier tag: short/medium/long rather than continuous bucketing.
- When switching fused-op status, use double-buffering for descriptors to allow inflight kernels to complete without global fence where possible.
- Introduce a metric in Console: kernel-churn-rate (kernel handoffs per minute per-GPU) and correlate with p99 regressions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Added grouping delay might violate 50ms latency SLO for short-tail customers. Mitigate by exempting routes with strict SLO or using dynamic thresholds based on route SLA tags.
- Risk: Extra prefetch increases memory pressure. Mitigate by making prefetch budget account for per-GPU free memory and token-weighted expected usage.

Appendix: selected raw snippets from traces (sanitized)
- example microtrace line:
  ts=1700002345.213 hostq enqueue id=abc123 prefix=12 gen_target=1024 chosen_kernel="flashpaged_v2" fused_path="no-fuse" kv_prefetch=1 kernel_switch=1
- gpu kernel launch sample:
  launch: flashattention_fused_ln_mm shadow_ms=0.24 occupancy=0.78 regs=128 shared=64 l2_miss_rate=0.012

Session notes (informal):
- Diego: "we definitely see the kernel fence right after the long req lands — the host shows 2ms stall to rebinding descriptors"
- Ruth: "quantized kernels are brittle around buffer layouts. If we expose a minimal view the fused kernel can accept both layouts with a small branching cost"
- Liam: "Console metric for kernel-churn will make this actionable for SRE; want to add alerting when churn correlates with p99 > target"

Bottom line:
Sequence-affinity grouping + selective FlashPaged priming reduces kernel churn and p99 for mixed-length workloads substantially in our tests. Next steps are to stress the change under higher QPS, harden fused-op layout tolerance, and add runtime metrics to make the behavior observable in Dedicated clusters.
